plan.mechanism: FP16-rounded gate has only 65536 encodings. Generate its FP32 SiLU values once per FFN call and reuse a 256KiB table inside the GEMM epilogue. No persistent GPU tensor cache.
plan.included_costs: Fresh table allocation and generation, GEMM/SwiGLU output allocation, quantization and q/scale allocation.

ffn_quantizer.decision: Do not promote any candidate to production
ffn_quantizer.conclusion: All four candidates preserve q and scale bits on one real FFN capture and synthetic edge inputs. Single-row 4-warps saves only 0.81% at real M7188 and one of three paired blocks regresses; 16-warps and both multirow variants are slower. The repeated-row M14376 extension is not an independent capture. No full-decode speedup has been measured or claimed.
ffn_quantizer.kernel_contract: Keep FP32 absmax and FP32 stored scales, FP16 denominator rounding, tl.div_rn, FP16 quotient rounding, nearbyint, NaN->-128, and INT8 clamp exactly unchanged.
mechanism_observations: Production single-row quantizer uses 54 registers/thread and 32 bytes shared memory at 8 warps; multirow variants increase register demand and shared reduction storage, with zero spills in these measurements. These resource counts alone do not establish a hardware bottleneck.

A real M7188 call reads 117768192 FP16 activation bytes and writes 58884096 INT8 bytes plus scales. Measured effective streaming traffic is approximately 1 TB/s; this is bytes divided by elapsed time, not a measured DRAM-bandwidth counter.

Fusing final rowwise quantization into current FFN-up tiles would require the exact maximum over 128 independent column tiles. A partial-max scratch would add producer work and another memory dependency while keeping the activation read/write pass. Do not implement this without evidence that reduction cost dominates.
